cli.permissions.help.permissions: Inspect or set up the macOS privacy identity Local Operator runtimes use
cli.permissions.help.status: Show which identity runtimes use and whether Screen Recording is granted (read-only)
cli.permissions.help.setup: Sign runtimes with your Developer ID so they share the desktop app's permissions (interactive)
cli.permissions.status.not_macos: macOS privacy permissions do not apply on this platform.
cli.permissions.status.identity.team: Runtime identity: {identifier}, sharing the desktop app's "Local Operator" row
cli.permissions.status.identity.adhoc: Runtime identity: {identifier}, its own "Local Operator Runtime" row
cli.permissions.status.identity.legacy: Runtime identity: a path-keyed image (no bundle could be built here), so each Python build is its own row
cli.permissions.status.identity.none: Runtime identity: not created yet; it is created the next time a runtime starts
cli.permissions.status.optin.off: Team signing: off. Run `lop permissions setup` to share the desktop app's row.
cli.permissions.status.optin.blocked: Team signing: unavailable in this process ({reason})
cli.permissions.status.screen.denied: Screen Recording (runtime preflight): not granted. Turn on "{row}" in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen Recording.
cli.permissions.status.screen.unknown: Screen Recording (runtime preflight): could not be checked
cli.permissions.setup.refused.tty: `lop permissions setup` is interactive. Run it in a terminal.
cli.permissions.setup.refused.isolated: Team signing is not allowed in this process ({reason}). Run it from your own login shell.
cli.permissions.setup.no_app: The Local Operator desktop app is not installed, so there is no app permission to share.
cli.permissions.setup.no_identity: No "Developer ID Application" signing identity for team {team} is in your keychain. Runtimes keep the "Local Operator Runtime" row.
cli.permissions.setup.explain: This signs the runtime with "{name}" so runtimes share the desktop app's privacy permissions. macOS may ask once whether codesign may use that key. Choose "Always Allow" so later `lop update` runs can sign without asking.
cli.permissions.setup.failed: Signing did not finish. Runtimes keep the "Local Operator Runtime" row. Run `lop permissions status` for details.
cli.permissions.setup.always_allow: Did you choose "Always Allow" (or did no dialog appear)? [y/N]
cli.permissions.setup.done: Done. New runtimes use {identifier} and share the desktop app's row. Running sessions keep their current image until they restart.
